another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the child (or children) you're claiming for.

**First question: How old is your child?**

This is important because:
- Children **under 16** generally qualify automatically (subject to other conditions)
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** are not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me your child's age, and if you have multiple children, let me know about each of them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and wanted to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm here to help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

So Alex is **16 years old**. At this age, eligibility depends on whether Alex is in approved education or training.

Let me ask you: **Is Alex currently enrolled in approved education or training?**

This would typically include:
- Full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels, T-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQ level 3 or below)
- Approved vocational training programs
- The education/training must be for at least 12 hours per week of supervised study or course-related work experience

Is Alex in this type of education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education at the moment. They finished school but haven't started anything yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex isn't currently in education or training.

Before I can determine the eligibility, I need to understand the timing a bit better. Child Benefit can sometimes continue for a limited period after education ends, depending on the circumstances.

**When did Alex finish school or leave their last education/training program?**

Also, **are they planning to start or continue education or training soon?**

This is important because there may be extension periods that apply in certain situations, such as:
- A short gap between leaving school and starting further education/training
- The period after finishing one course and before starting another
- Time after turning 16 but before the relevant date when education/training starts

Could you tell me more about Alex's situation and timing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex left school a few months ago, back in the summer. They're not really sure what they want to do next - still figuring things out, you know? They haven't signed up for anything specific yet or registered with careers services or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail. I understand Alex is taking some time to figure out their next steps.

Based on what you've told me, let me work through the eligibility rules:

**For 16-19 year olds**, Child Benefit continues **only if** the young person is in approved education or training. Since Alex:
- Is 16 years old
- Left school a few months ago (in the summer)
- Is not currently enrolled in any education or training
- Hasn't registered for approved training or with careers services
- Has no immediate plans to start education/training

Let me navigate to the appropriate outcome based on this situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex might qualify for an extension period. Let me ask one more specific question:

**How many weeks has it been since Alex left school?**

This is important because there may be an extension period of up to 20 weeks after leaving education in certain circumstances. If it's been:
- Less than 20 weeks AND Alex is registered or enrolled to start education/training, there might be an extension
- More than 20 weeks, or not planning to continue education/training, then unfortunately Alex wouldn't qualify

Can you tell me approximately when in the summer Alex left school?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was back in June when school finished - so that would be about... let me think... around 5 or 6 months ago now, I suppose.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So it's been approximately 5-6 months (around 20-24 weeks) since Alex left school in June.

Let me check the extension eligibility rules to be thorough.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can now see the specific rule. For the extension period to apply, two conditions must be met:

1. The child must have left approved education within the **last 20 weeks**, AND
2. They must be registered with a qualifying service (government careers service, Connexions, or armed services)

In Alex's case:
- It's been **5-6 months (approximately 20-24 weeks)** since leaving school - which is beyond the 20-week limit
- Alex **hasn't registered** with careers services or any qualifying service

Since both conditions aren't met, the extension doesn't apply.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Your Child Benefit Eligibility Result

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why this decision was made:

For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit only continues if they are in **approved education or training**. Since Alex:
- Left school approximately 5-6 months ago (June)
- Is not currently enrolled in education or training
- Has not registered with a careers service or qualifying program

Alex does not meet the qualifying child criteria.

### About the Extension Period:

There is a **20-week extension** available for 16-17 year olds who leave education, but only if they register with:
- A government careers service
- Connexions service  
- Armed services

Unfortunately, since Alex hasn't registered with any of these services and it's now been over 20 weeks since leaving school, this extension period doesn't apply.

### What happens now:

If you were receiving Child Benefit for Alex, it would have stopped after the extension period ended. You should inform HMRC if you're still receiving payments.

### Good news for the future:

**If Alex enrolls in approved education or training**, you could become eligible again! This includes:
- A-levels, T-levels, or Scottish Highers
- NVQ level 3 or below
- Approved vocational training (at least 12 hours per week)

If Alex decides to go back into education or training, you can make a new claim at that time.

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or Alex's situation?
